about: The HAND-KEPT part of the liveness manifest: log lines a healthy boot must print, matched by regex. dev/loud/gen_liveness.js copies `entries` into dev/loud/liveness_manifest.json (the file loud-check.ps1 reads); the ARMED ids and the FIRED names of that file are generated from the scripts and are not listed here.

A line belongs here only when it proves something the generated set does not. `proves` says which: handler-ran (printed inside a load-time handler: the event was posted and the handler got there; the checker's `notfired:` finding says the same at AMBER since 2026-10-13, and these lines stay until it has been live for a few boots), own-check (a `must_not` line or a `min` floor), direct-registry (a handler put straight on a Java registry of the mod, which has no id), no-registration (a script that only publishes a table), mixin (an in-house mixin applied), corpus (a load-time line that the replay corpus needs: see its `why`). `why` is the sentence for that entry.

Rules, unchanged: (1) an entry names its owner, so a commit that deletes or renames a feature removes or updates its entry (the generator refuses an entry whose owner script is gone); (2) `pattern` is a .NET regex searched in each line of `log`; script lines carry their own script path, which is part of the pattern; (3) `must_not` lists lines that mean the feature failed even though its line printed; (4) `min` is a floor for the first capture group of `pattern`.
A NEW script needs no entry: write its registrations with icraft.guard / registerServerTick / core.onHurt and regenerate. Add a line here only for one of the first five reasons above.

`dropped` records the 134-entry manifest of 2026-10-11: the entries that were removed on 2026-10-13 when the ARMED set became generated, each with the reason. `node --expose-internals dev/loud/gen_liveness.js --lines` prints where every kept line is printed and what its script registers.
